baselineName: keyword lists (top 8 per class by log-odds, fit split only)

clauseType.instructions: This is one provision from a commercial contract. What does this provision mainly do?

criteria.governingLaw: Chooses which jurisdiction's law will be used to interpret and enforce the agreement
criteria.notices: Sets out how formal communications between the parties must be delivered: in writing, by which method, to which address, and when they count as received
criteria.entireAgreement: Declares that the written agreement is the complete deal between the parties and replaces any earlier agreements, promises or understandings on the same subject
criteria.amendment: Sets out how the agreement (or part of it) can be changed, altered or modified, such as only by a signed writing or by a particular party
criteria.termination: Ends the agreement or a relationship, or sets out when and how it ends or may be ended and what happens at that point
criteria.assignment: Controls whether a party may transfer its rights or obligations under the agreement to someone else, and on what conditions
criteria.confidentiality: Requires a party to keep certain information secret or restricts how that information may be used or disclosed
criteria.indemnification: Requires one party to compensate, reimburse, hold harmless or defend another party for losses, claims, liabilities or expenses
criteria.other: Does something else: any other kind of provision (for example payment, representations, severability, counterparts, taxes, dispute venue), or none of the above is its main purpose

namesJurisdiction.instructions: Does the provision name a specific U.S. state, country or other jurisdiction (for example "the State of Delaware", "New York", "England and Wales")?

saysAgreementEnds.instructions: Does the provision say that the agreement, or a party's rights or obligations under it, ends, terminates or may be terminated?

requiresCoveringLosses.instructions: Does the provision require one party to pay for, reimburse, hold harmless or defend another party against losses, claims, damages or expenses?

restrictsDisclosure.instructions: Does the provision forbid or limit a party from disclosing or using certain information?
